function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **root** of the `nodejs-welcome` repository.  
I’ve written the files so they work out‑of‑the‑box for a typical Node.js web app that listens on port 3000.  

> **NOTE** – I don’t have direct access to your machine or the repo, so I can’t actually run the `git clone`, `git add`, `git commit`, or `git push` commands for you.  
> Instead, I’ll give you the exact file contents and the shell commands you need to run locally (or in a CI job) to finish the task.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repo

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Create the required files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the repo root with the following content:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy only the files needed for installing dependencies
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Build step (if you have a build script)
# RUN npm run build

# Final stage
FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Copy built artifacts from the builder stage
COPY --from=builder /app .

EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *Why this Dockerfile?*  
> - Uses the lightweight `node:18-alpine` image.  
> - Builds in a separate stage so the final image only contains what’s needed at runtime.  
> - Exposes port 3000 (the common default for Node.js apps).  
> - Starts the app with `node app.js`. Adjust the entrypoint if your main file is named differently (`index.js`, `server.js`, etc.).

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file named `k8s.yaml` (or split into `deployment.yaml` & `service.yaml`) with the following content:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your image name
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to NodePort or ClusterIP if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80                  # External port
    targetPort: 3000          # Container port
```

> **Tip** – If you’re deploying to a cluster that doesn’t support `LoadBalancer` (e.g., Minikube), change `type: LoadBalancer` to `NodePort`.

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml` with the following content:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build_and_push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to DockerHub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Cache Docker layers
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: /tmp/.buildx-cache
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-${{ github.sha }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        file: ./Dockerfile
        push: true
        tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What you need to set up first**  
> 1. In your GitHub repo → Settings → Secrets → Actions → New repository secret  
>    - `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`: Your Docker Hub username  
>    - `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`: A Docker Hub personal access token (with `write:packages` scope)  
> 2. Optionally, add a `DOCKERHUB_PASSWORD` secret if you prefer to use username/password instead of a token.

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s.yaml .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically trigger on the `push` event, building and pushing the Docker image to Docker Hub.

---

## 🎉 What you now have

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a minimal, production‑ready Docker image for your Node.js app. |
| `k8s.yaml` | Deploys two replicas of your app behind a LoadBalancer service. |
| `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml` | Automates Docker image build & push on every push to `main`. |

Feel free to tweak the image name, number of replicas, or service type to suit your environment. Happy coding!
